user.title: Reolink Stamina
user.description:
Adds a **Reolink Events** panel to the sidebar for reviewing events recorded by your Reolink devices.

There is nothing to configure: devices and cameras are discovered through the official Reolink integration, and no camera credentials are stored.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Reolink Stamina is already set up.
abort.no_nvr: No Reolink NVR is set up in the Reolink integration. Reolink Stamina only works with a recorder, so there is nothing for it to show yet.

init.title: Reolink Stamina
init.description: What is switched on. The next pages cover the player, and anything a switched-on feature needs.

data_description.hide_timer: On: person, vehicle and animal, with motion as a filter. Off also brings back scheduled and unlabelled recordings, which dominate a 24/7 recorder.
data_description.require_admin: Recordings can be sensitive. Off lets non-admin users open the panel.
data_description.verify_tls: Off suits the self-signed certificate Reolink ships, which no verification can pass. On only if you installed one this Home Assistant trusts.
data_description.beta_restream: Converts a recording when the browser cannot play it — H.265 on Chrome or Firefox, or anything on an iPhone. Needs ffmpeg.
data_description.beta_all_devices: Lists Home Hubs and cameras with their own SD card. Untested hardware, hence beta.
data_description.beta_relevance: Marks the events that are unusual for a camera, by counting what it normally sees. Nothing is recorded until you turn this on, it stays on this machine, and removing the integration deletes it.

signals.title: Marking, and what else to count
signals.description:
Relevance already counts the time of day, how long a detection lasted, which camera fired before it, and what each camera reports about itself — its floodlight, its siren, and its day/night state, which is the camera telling you it switched to infrared. Those are found automatically and attached to the camera they belong to.

Add anything here that is true of the whole property rather than of one lens: whether anybody is in, whether the alarm is set, whether the gate is locked. "A person on the drive while nobody is home" then becomes its own thing rather than just a person on the drive.

One list per recorder, because a Home Assistant often covers more than one property. Leaving them empty is fine.

data_description.relevance_sensitivity: A row is marked when it is unusual for its camera and unusual at all. This moves the second of those. Measured across nine cameras, the three choices came out at roughly 1.6, 4 and 9 marks a day for the whole property. Change it whenever — nothing is recounted, the line just moves.

player.title: The player
player.description: How recordings are searched, trimmed and played.

data.clip_lead: Clip: seconds before the first detection
data.clip_tail: Clip: seconds after the last detection

data_description.browse_stream: Low resolution searches faster. Playback and downloads can still use high.
data_description.split_minutes: How finely long recordings split into rows. 0 lists one row per file.
data_description.pre_roll: Where to draw the trigger marker for cameras that do not report their own.
data_description.event_lead: Where the playhead opens inside the clip. It does not change the clip.
data_description.clip_lead: On 24/7 footage, where a trimmed clip starts before the first detection.
data_description.clip_tail: And where it ends, after the last one clears.

reolink_incompatible.title: Reolink Stamina cannot read the Reolink integration
reolink_incompatible.description:
The installed Reolink integration no longer exposes its connection the way this panel expects, so events cannot be listed.

This usually means Home Assistant was updated and the panel needs updating too. Check for an update to Reolink Stamina, and open an issue if there is none.

user.title: Sync clips to the cloud
user.description: Uploads a clip for every detection on this recorder's cameras, as soon as it has finished writing it. One cloud sync per NVR.

data_description.nvr_entry_id: Clips are uploaded for every camera on this Reolink NVR. Recorders that already have a cloud sync are not listed.
data_description.destination_entry_id: An existing OneDrive integration. Its credentials are reused, so there is nothing to authorise again; clips go into Home Assistant's own app folder.
data_description.quota_gb: How much this recorder's clips may occupy. Once full, the oldest clips are deleted to make room for new ones.
data_description.kinds: Motion fires constantly on most cameras and will spend the quota on empty footage; person, vehicle and animal are the useful ones.
data_description.sync_stream: Low resolution is a fraction of the size and plays everywhere.
data_description.sync_lead: How much footage to keep before the first detection.
data_description.sync_tail: How much to keep after the last detection clears.
data_description.remote_folder: Where clips are stored, as `folder/240102_153045_recorder_camera.mp4`. May be several levels deep.

reconfigure.title: Cloud sync settings
reconfigure.description: Which recorder this syncs is fixed. To sync a different one, add a cloud sync for it.

data_description.quota_gb: How much this recorder's clips may occupy. Once full, the oldest clips are deleted to make room for new ones.
data_description.kinds: Motion fires constantly on most cameras and will spend the quota on empty footage; person, vehicle and animal are the useful ones.

data_description.sync_lead: How much footage to keep before the first detection.
data_description.sync_tail: How much to keep after the last detection clears.
